In 1604 Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, finished the Adi Granth, the first form of the Sikh scripture, and installed it in the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar.

He gathered the hymns of the first five Gurus, starting with Guru Nanak, and had them written out by the scribe Bhai Gurdas. He also included hymns by saints from outside the Sikh fold:

  • Kabir, the weaver poet of Varanasi.
  • Namdev and Ravidas, low caste Hindu devotees.
  • Baba Farid, a Muslim Sufi of the Punjab.

The hymns are set to musical modes and written in the Gurmukhi script. Including Hindu and Muslim saints said plainly that devotion to the one God mattered more than birth or creed.

Two years later Guru Arjan was executed under the Mughal emperor Jahangir. The tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, added the hymns of his father and, before his death in 1708, declared the book itself the eternal Guru. As the Guru Granth Sahib it stands at the centre of every gurdwara and of Sikhism.
sum: In 1604 Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, finished the Adi Granth, the first form of the Sikh scripture, and installed it in the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar.
